- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use moving average to dampen.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often holds or overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% prior, 30% sentiment) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +1, –1, +1), model often misaligns with true trend; favor trend-following with sentiment lag of 2–3 days.
